body:
#2066 (SPIKE-85) APPROVED AT ac772eaca9. All five criteria met and verified against the tree rather than read back from the report.

C1 does the hardest thing the spec asked. The predicate is stated narrowly with inclusions and exclusions, AND its boundary is named: "silently presenting it as exhaustive would reproduce the defect under study." A sweep for self-referential blindness claiming completeness would have been instance seven in its own first paragraph.

C3 verified in the store: BUG-1578 exists as a draft bug with a matching title. The bundling argument is sound - one workflow condition, one fix boundary. And three NON-findings are explicitly not filed, with the reason stated: "no bug was filed without a reproducible failure."

C4 I checked rather than assumed, because a re-run block citing a script that does not exist is worth nothing. ALL THIRTEEN referenced paths resolve. I also re-derived the marker count independently: 21 sites, matching the report exactly.

C5 answered as a decision, not an omission - "not safely automatable as a general lint" - and no lint was added. The spec warned that automating it would be instance seven; the report declined.

THE CORROBORATION THE REPORT DOES NOT CLAIM, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN IT. BUG-1578 says docs-only PRs suppress the documentation drift guards. THIS PR IS DOCS-ONLY. I verified the mechanism end to end: ci.yml's `full_ci` filter is inverted and excludes `docs/**` and `**/*.md` (lines 52-58); this PR's sole file matches both; and four doc gates are gated on `full_ci == 'true'` - External-prose classifier inventory (:147), MCP doc-consistency (:184), Doc-intent gate (:266), CLI-manual drift-guard (:297).

So the four doc gates did not run on the artifact reporting that they do not run. The finding demonstrated itself, on its own PR, while being reported. That is better evidence for BUG-1578 than the inventory row that produced it, and I suggested as non-blocking that one sentence be added - it converts an inspected claim into a reproduced one. I did not hold the PR for it.

MERGE CONDITION RECORDED, NOT AN OBJECTION: this PR was approved with its governing gates skipped. For THIS document that costs nothing - it cites no CLI surface, adds no command, asserts no tool descriptor. I recorded it because that should be a stated condition rather than a silent one, and because it will not be harmless on the next docs-only PR that touches a governed document.

NOW #2067 (BUG-1511), WHICH IS NOT ROUTED TO ME. I looked only because it adds a file to a PUBLIC repo, and that is worth a check even unrouted. ON THE CONFIDENTIALITY QUESTION IT IS CLEAN: the tracked `.codex/config.toml` is three lines registering the MCP server - no secrets, no machine paths, no employer context - and it is the correct twin of the tracked `.mcp.json`. The named-entries-not-a-glob choice is right for the reason the diff gives.

ONE FORWARD-LOOKING GAP, AND I NEARLY REPORTED THE OPPOSITE. The PR ignores `/.codex/hooks.json`, justified as "wires local hooks with ABSOLUTE machine paths". My first check said that file contains ZERO absolute paths, which would have made the justification false. THAT WAS MY BAD GREP - I matched `"/`, assuming a path starts immediately after a quote, but the paths sit inside larger command strings. They ARE absolute. The justification holds and I would have filed a false finding on a pattern error.

Checking it properly is what found the real thing: HOOKS.JSON WIRES EIGHT SHELL SCRIPTS UNDER `.codex/hooks/` - aida-advisor-code-guard.sh, aida-capture-prompt.sh, aida-git-guardrails.sh, aida-mail-notice.sh, aida-role-context.sh, aida-session-context.sh, aida-subagent-start.sh, aida-subagent-stop.sh - and the PR's rules cover the MANIFEST but not the DIRECTORY the manifest points at. `.codex/hooks/` is empty on this machine right now, so nothing is publishable today and this is not a blocker. But those scripts are machine-local wiring by the PR's own classification, and the day one is scaffolded or arrives from another machine it lands untracked-and-unignored - which is precisely the state the PR's own CLAUDE.md text names as the one that `git add -A` publishes from.

It is the day's shape again: THE RULE COVERS THE INSTANCE IT SAW, NOT THE CATEGORY. The author was looking at hooks.json because hooks.json was in the dirty tree; the eight scripts it references were not, because the directory is empty here. One line - `/.codex/hooks/` - closes it, and the decision is the same one the PR already made and documented for hooks.json.

Routing it to you rather than recording a verdict, since #2067 is not mine.
subject: #2066 APPROVED — and it demonstrates BUG-1578 on itself; plus a gap on unrouted #2067: hooks.json is ignored, the 8 scripts it wires are not
